categories.title: State of Minnesota hiring and inclusion programs
categories.intro: The State of Minnesota runs its own hiring paths for people with disabilities, veterans and students, and its employees run resource groups. These programs can bring candidates into Department of Human Services jobs and connect staff with colleagues across agencies.

entries.name: State of Minnesota Careers
entries.what: Minnesota Management and Budget's site where all state agency jobs, student worker positions and internships are posted, with job alerts for applicants.
entries.howToUse: Post Department of Human Services openings and point candidates to job alerts.

entries.name: Connect 700 Program
entries.what: A non-competitive path into state jobs for people with certain disabilities, with an on-the-job trial of up to 700 hours; Minnesota Management and Budget published its 2026 program report.
entries.howToUse: Mark eligible openings as Connect 700 and share the eligibility application with disability partners.

entries.name: Supported Worker Program
entries.what: State program, under Minnesota Statutes 43A.421, in which up to 50 full-time state positions can be shared by people with significant disabilities, with job coach support; the statute was amended in 2025.
entries.howToUse: Work with agency human resources to place a supported worker position in a Department of Human Services team.

entries.name: Executive Pathways Internship Program
entries.what: Paid summer internship at the Department of Human Services for sophomores and graduate students, 30 to 40 hours a week from June to August, telework eligible in Minnesota.
entries.howToUse: Host interns and share the program with college career offices.

entries.name: Minnesota Department of Transportation SEEDS Student Worker Program
entries.what: Year-round paid student worker program at the Minnesota Department of Transportation for college students in related majors, with workshops; a 2026 winter workshop was held.
entries.howToUse: Use as a model for student worker pathways and refer students in human services-related majors to state student worker openings.

entries.name: Veterans Preference and Recently Separated Veterans Hiring
entries.what: State hiring rules that rank qualified veterans ahead of other applicants, guarantee interviews to the top five qualified recently separated veterans, and allow non-competitive hiring of veterans with a service-connected disability of 30 percent or more.
entries.howToUse: Apply these rules when filling Department of Human Services openings and tell veteran applicants about them.

entries.name: Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs Employment Resources
entries.what: Lists employment resources for veterans and a section for businesses, and partners with the Department of Employment and Economic Development on veterans job services.
entries.howToUse: Use its business resources and share Department of Human Services openings with veterans.

entries.name: CareerForce Veterans Employment Program
entries.what: Department of Employment and Economic Development staff at CareerForce locations who help veterans find jobs and help employers recruit veterans.
entries.howToUse: Contact a local Veterans Employment Representative to recruit veterans.

entries.name: Minnesota Veterans Career Fair
entries.what: Yearly career fair held by the Department of Employment and Economic Development and the Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs; the 20th fair on May 20, 2026, in Brooklyn Center had 100 employers.
entries.howToUse: Register as an employer for the next fair to meet veteran job seekers.

entries.name: State of Minnesota Enterprise Employee Resource Groups
entries.what: Employee-led groups open to all state employees, including Black, Indigenous, Women of Color; Equity Justice Black Caucus; Employees of Asian Descent; Employees with Disabilities; Jewish Culture and Heritage; MNclusive; Next Gen; and Parents at Work.
entries.howToUse: Invite the groups to share Department of Human Services job openings with members and to take part in listening sessions.

categories.title: Workforce centers and job training organizations
categories.intro: Workforce centers and community job training organizations prepare and place job seekers, including people with disabilities, immigrants and refugees, and residents of Greater Minnesota. Many have staff who connect employers with trained candidates at no cost.

entries.name: CareerForce
entries.what: Minnesota's public workforce system, run by the Department of Employment and Economic Development with local partners, with locations across the state. Employer services, including job posting, recruiting and job fairs, are free.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs on the state job bank, submit hiring events, and work with regional employer services staff.

entries.name: Vocational Rehabilitation Services, Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development
entries.what: Helps people with disabilities prepare for and find work. Its Business Consultants serve employers in every region, with statewide specialists for Deaf and Hard of Hearing job seekers and for blind job seekers.
entries.howToUse: Contact a regional Business Consultant to recruit candidates with disabilities and get help with accommodations.

entries.name: State Services for the Blind
entries.what: Helps people who are blind, have low vision or are DeafBlind find and keep jobs. Its Workforce Development Unit works with employers on hiring and accommodations, with offices around the state.
entries.howToUse: Contact the Workforce Development Unit to recruit candidates and plan accommodations.

entries.name: Twin Cities R!SE
entries.what: Free eight-week career training, personal empowerment training and two years of coaching for people facing barriers to work; active in 2026.
entries.howToUse: Partner as an employer to hire program graduates.

entries.name: Summit Academy OIC
entries.what: Accredited career and technical training center in North Minneapolis offering 20-week programs, including Medical Administrative Assistant and IT Specialist, plus GED classes; held its 2026 commencement.
entries.howToUse: Hire graduates through its employer partner program or request a tour.

entries.name: Goodwill-Easter Seals Minnesota
entries.what: Provides free career training, industry training and employment services, with a Career and Services Campus in St. Paul and locations around the state.
entries.howToUse: Work with its employment services to hire training graduates.

entries.name: International Institute of Minnesota
entries.what: Provides free classes, job training and career advancement for immigrants and refugees, with staff who speak 28 languages; received Department of Employment and Economic Development training grants in January 2026.
entries.howToUse: Use its Hire Our Clients program to recruit trained immigrant and refugee candidates.

entries.name: CAPI USA
entries.what: Serves immigrants and refugees in the Twin Cities with workforce training and financial education; services moved to its Immigrant Opportunity Center in Brooklyn Center in September 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share job openings with its workforce training participants.

entries.name: Lao Assistance Center of Minnesota
entries.what: Serves Lao and other Asian American and Pacific Islander communities in the Twin Cities and rural Minnesota with help on housing, employment and education barriers; held events in fall 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share job and service announcements with Lao families and partner on community events.

entries.name: Hmong American Partnership
entries.what: Serves Hmong and Southeast Asian American communities and other immigrants and refugees; its HAP Academy OIC offers career and technical training, employment services and adult education.
entries.howToUse: Share job openings with HAP Academy OIC job seekers.

entries.name: CLUES
entries.what: Latino-led nonprofit offering job training, employment and economic programs from St. Paul, Minneapolis, Willmar and Austin; it runs a CareerForce location on East Lake Street in Minneapolis.
entries.howToUse: Share job openings with its employment programs and partner on outreach to Latino communities.

entries.name: Neighborhood House
entries.what: St. Paul nonprofit serving refugees, immigrants and others in transition; its adult education program offers English, citizenship and career readiness classes, offered in person and online in 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share entry-level job openings with adult education learners.

entries.name: English Learning Center
entries.what: Free English, math and citizenship classes for adult immigrants and refugees in South Minneapolis, a program of Our Saviour's Community Services.
entries.howToUse: Share job and service announcements with adult English learners.

entries.name: Karen Organization of Minnesota
entries.what: Serves refugee and immigrant communities, with a focus on Karen and other refugees from Burma; offers adult career pathways and employment supports in the Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota.
entries.howToUse: Share job openings with its career pathways participants and partner on outreach to Karen communities.

entries.name: Rural Minnesota CEP
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: Northwest and West Central
entries.what: Workforce provider in the CareerForce system with offices in Alexandria, Bemidji, Brainerd, Detroit Lakes, Fergus Falls, Little Falls, Moorhead and Wadena; posted fall 2026 news and an employer webinar.
entries.howToUse: Use its business services to recruit job seekers in northwest and west central Minnesota.

entries.name: Southwest Minnesota Private Industry Council
entries.what: Workforce provider for 14 southwest Minnesota counties with CareerForce offices in Marshall, Montevideo and Worthington; scheduled November 2026 sessions for laid-off workers.
entries.howToUse: Use its talent acquisition services to recruit job seekers in southwest Minnesota.

entries.name: Central Minnesota Jobs and Training Services
entries.what: Workforce provider for 11 central Minnesota counties, from Chisago to Renville, connecting businesses with qualified workers through its business services and talent portal.
entries.howToUse: Use its business services and talent portal to recruit job seekers in central Minnesota.

entries.name: JET - Northeast Minnesota Office of Job Training
entries.what: Workforce provider with offices in Aitkin, Carlton, Duluth, Grand Rapids, Hibbing, International Falls and Virginia, offering hiring assistance and wage reimbursement to employers.
entries.howToUse: Use its hiring assistance to recruit job seekers in northeast Minnesota.

categories.title: Colleges and universities
categories.intro: Minnesota colleges and universities train the social workers, human services workers, interpreters, nurses and public health staff the Department of Human Services hires. Their programs, career offices and job fairs are direct routes to students and recent graduates.

entries.name: University of Minnesota Twin Cities School of Social Work
entries.what: Offers a Master of Social Work in full-program, advanced standing and online formats; the first online cohort began in fall 2026. Students complete 600 to 1,020 practicum hours.
entries.howToUse: Offer practicum placements and post social work openings to students and recent graduates through the University's Handshake job system.

entries.name: University of Minnesota School of Public Health Career Services
entries.what: Career office for public health students. Employers post jobs and internships in Handshake and can attend its Career Connect event (spring 2026 event held February 12, 2026) at no cost.
entries.howToUse: Post public health jobs and internships, host an applied practice experience, or attend Career Connect.

entries.name: University of Minnesota Career Services
entries.what: Runs the University's Handshake job system and the career fairs held across its colleges and campuses; fall 2026 fairs were held in September. Its site has a channel for students with disabilities.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs in Handshake and register for University career fairs, including the system-wide Job and Internship Fair.

entries.name: Institute on Community Integration, University of Minnesota
entries.what: Research and training center on disability and community living. It publishes on the direct support workforce and runs 2026-27 online trainings for direct support workers in Minnesota's consumer-directed programs.
entries.howToUse: Share workforce announcements with its direct support networks and use its published training for direct support workers.

entries.name: University of Minnesota Duluth Department of Social Work
entries.what: Offers Bachelor and Master of Social Work degrees; applications for the 2027-28 Master of Social Work open October 15, 2026, and a fully online track begins fall 2027.
entries.howToUse: Offer field placements and share job openings with social work students in northeast Minnesota.

entries.name: Minnesota State University, Mankato Department of Social Work
entries.what: Offers a Bachelor of Science in Social Work and a Master of Social Work, both accredited by the Council on Social Work Education, listed in the 2026-27 catalog.
entries.howToUse: Offer field placements and share job openings with social work students in southern Minnesota.

entries.name: Minnesota State University Moorhead Social Work Program
entries.what: Offers on-campus and online Bachelor of Social Work degrees, with a 480-hour internship, and an online Master of Social Work.
entries.howToUse: Offer internship placements and share job openings with social work students in northwest Minnesota.

entries.name: Bemidji State University Social Work Program
entries.what: Offers on-campus and hybrid Bachelor of Social Work degrees, with 540 hours of practice in a human service organization; admission dates are posted for fall 2026 and spring 2027.
entries.howToUse: Offer practice placements and share job openings with social work students in north central Minnesota.

entries.name: Winona State University College of Nursing and Health Sciences
entries.what: Offers Bachelor of Social Work degrees in Winona and Rochester, an online Master of Social Work focused on trauma-informed practice, and accredited nursing degrees.
entries.howToUse: Offer practicum placements and share social work and nursing openings with students in southeast Minnesota.

entries.name: Saint Paul College Sign Language Interpreter/Transliterator Program
entries.what: Associate of Applied Science degree in American Sign Language-English interpreting; the fall 2026 application is open. The college also offers American Sign Language Studies.
entries.howToUse: Share interpreter job openings and internship placements with interpreting students.

entries.name: Minneapolis College Human Services Program
entries.what: Offers a Human Services diploma and an Associate of Science degree with community service and fieldwork, plus addiction counseling and mental health worker programs.
entries.howToUse: Offer fieldwork sites and share entry-level human services openings with students.

entries.name: Rochester Community and Technical College Human Services and Nursing Programs
entries.what: Offers human services certificates, including Developmental Disabilities Assistant and Mental Health Assistant, a Human Services Specialist degree, and an Associate Degree Nursing program that held its 2026 pinning ceremony.
entries.howToUse: Share direct support, human services and nursing openings with students and graduates.

entries.name: St. Catherine University ASL and Interpreting Department and CATIE Center
entries.what: Offers an accredited ASL-English interpreting degree. Its CATIE Center runs federally funded projects for new Deaf and hearing interpreters and for healthcare interpreting with Deaf, Hard of Hearing and DeafBlind patients.
entries.howToUse: Share interpreter job openings and internship placements with students and with the CATIE Center's interpreter cohorts.

entries.name: University of St. Thomas School of Social Work
entries.what: Part of the Morrison Family College of Health; offers Bachelor, Master and Doctor of Social Work degrees, with 2026-27 handbooks and admission dates posted.
entries.howToUse: Offer field placements and share social work openings with students and graduates.

entries.name: Augsburg University Master of Social Work Program
entries.what: Master of Social Work program that received a five-year federal grant in October 2026 for scholarships tied to later work in medically underserved communities. Augsburg also offers a Master of Science in Nursing.
entries.howToUse: Offer field placements and share social work openings with students who commit to work in underserved communities.

entries.name: Minnesota Private Colleges Job and Internship Fair
entries.what: Yearly job fair for sophomores, juniors and seniors from Minnesota private colleges; the 2026 fair was held February 18, 2026, and the 2027 fair is set for February 23, 2027, at the Minneapolis Convention Center. Government and social services employers take part.
entries.howToUse: Register as an employer to meet students from private colleges across Minnesota.

categories.title: Professional associations and networks
categories.intro: Professional associations and networks reach people already working in social work, human services, disability services, interpreting, human resources and nonprofits. Many offer job boards, newsletters, conferences and events where employers can connect with members.

entries.name: National Association of Social Workers, Minnesota Chapter
entries.what: Professional association for social workers in Minnesota, with regional networking events, webinars and a winter virtual conference; posted news in November 2026.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs or promote openings through its website and member newsletter, and attend its events.

entries.name: Minnesota Social Service Association
entries.what: Association for health and human services professionals since 1893, with regional fall conferences in November 2026, an advocacy day, and a 2027 Annual Conference and Expo.
entries.howToUse: Exhibit at its conference and expo and attend regional conferences to meet county and community human services staff.

entries.name: Minnesota Council of Nonprofits
entries.what: Statewide association of nonprofits that runs Minnesota's largest nonprofit job board, trainings and conferences; published its 2026 report on the nonprofit sector.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs on its nonprofit job board and share announcements with nonprofit partners.

entries.name: Minnesota Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf
entries.what: Association of sign language interpreters, transliterators and consumers, with continuing education, an educational interpreter community of practice and a member email list; has a 2026 board.
entries.howToUse: Share interpreter job openings with members and attend its events.

entries.name: Minnesota State Council of the Society for Human Resource Management
entries.what: Links Minnesota's local chapters of the Society for Human Resource Management, including Twin Cities SHRM, which held its fall conference in November 2026; published the 2026 Minnesota HR Workforce Outlook Report.
entries.howToUse: Attend chapter events and the state conference to share inclusive hiring practices with other employers.

entries.name: Minnesota Association of Rehabilitation Providers
entries.what: Professional organization of qualified rehabilitation consultants and other rehabilitation providers in Minnesota; its next spring conference is April 9, 2027.
entries.howToUse: Attend its conferences to connect with rehabilitation professionals who place people in jobs.

entries.name: Minnesota APSE
entries.what: Network that promotes Employment First, competitive integrated employment for people with disabilities; held its 2026 state conference on October 8, 2026, in Shoreview.
entries.howToUse: Attend its conference and share disability hiring opportunities with its network.

entries.name: MOHR
entries.alsoKnownAs: Minnesota Organization for Habilitation and Rehabilitation
entries.what: Association of 97 organizations that provide employment and day supports to Minnesotans with disabilities in all 87 counties; posted news in October 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share announcements with member organizations and their staff.

entries.name: ARRM
entries.what: Association of home and community-based service providers for people with disabilities; runs a job board and events, including a Business and Finance Forum on November 18, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs on its job board and attend its forums.
entries.dhsRecord: ARRM lists a question-and-answer session with the Department of Human Services at its November 18, 2026 forum: https://www.arrm.org/

entries.name: Minnesota Public Health Association
entries.what: Association of public health professionals with an annual conference (April 2026 at St. Cloud State University), a 2026-27 policy forum series and committee meetings.
entries.howToUse: Attend its conference and forums to reach public health professionals.

entries.name: LatinoLEAD
entries.what: Network of more than 3,500 Latine professionals in Minnesota, with leadership programs and community events, including LIDERCON 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share job openings with its network and attend its events.

entries.name: The B Suite
entries.what: Minneapolis events and co-working hub for Black professionals, launched in 2023 and profiled in March 2026.
entries.howToUse: Attend or partner on its events to connect with Black professionals.

entries.name: People of Color Career Fair
entries.what: Career fair for professionals of color held each spring in Saint Paul and each fall in Minneapolis; the 16th fair was held April 28, 2026, at Saint Paul RiverCentre.
entries.howToUse: Register as an employer for an upcoming fair.

categories.title: Community and regional media
categories.intro: Newspapers, radio, television and online outlets that serve specific communities and regions of Minnesota. Many take paid advertising, classified or job ads, public service announcements or event listings, which can carry job openings and service information to people who may not see mainstream channels.

entries.name: Sahan Journal
entries.what: Nonprofit digital newsroom that reports for immigrants and communities of color in Minnesota. It runs a Spanish-language section, "Sahan en Español," and publishes daily.
entries.howToUse: Post openings on its job board, or place advertising or sponsored content through its advertising and sponsorship page.

entries.name: Minnesota Spokesman-Recorder
entries.what: Minnesota's oldest Black-owned newspaper, published weekly in print and online from Minneapolis. Its site has classifieds (jobs and notices), a bulletin section and a community events calendar.
entries.howToUse: Place job ads in its classifieds, buy advertising, or submit a community event free through its events page.

entries.name: Insight News
entries.what: North Minneapolis weekly that covers Black communities, Black-led nonprofits and small businesses. Its site has job and community classifieds and a local events calendar.
entries.howToUse: Post jobs in its job classifieds, share notices in its community classifieds, or promote an event through its events calendar.

entries.name: Mshale
entries.what: Minneapolis-based newspaper serving African immigrants in Minnesota, with a print edition and a website. Its site posted event coverage in 2026, and its latest print edition found was dated December 15, 2025.
entries.howToUse: Contact the publisher through the website about advertising or community coverage.

entries.name: Hmong Times
entries.what: Saint Paul newspaper for the Hmong community, founded in 1998 and now mainly online. Its site has a community section and an events calendar, and it offers a media kit for advertisers.
entries.howToUse: Request its media kit to advertise to Hmong readers, or check its events calendar for community gatherings.

entries.name: KFAI Fresh Air Community Radio
entries.what: Volunteer-based community radio station in Minneapolis. Its schedule includes programs made by and for Somali, Oromo, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Vietnamese and Filipino communities, and a disability program, "Disability and Progress."
entries.howToUse: Submit a public service announcement through its PSA form, or arrange underwriting through its underwriting page.

entries.name: KMOJ 89.9 FM
entries.what: North Minneapolis community radio station founded in 1976 that serves Minnesota's African American community. Its morning show and KMOJCast podcast carry community and public-service interviews.
entries.howToUse: Contact the station through its website about underwriting or community interview segments.

entries.name: KALY 101.7 FM Somali American Radio
entries.what: Somali-language radio station in Minneapolis serving Somali and East African immigrants, with local and international news and an event calendar.
entries.howToUse: Contact the station about underwriting or sharing community announcements on air.

entries.name: KRSM Radio For All 98.9 FM
entries.what: South Minneapolis low-power community station with shows in English, Spanish, Somali, Ojibwe and Haitian Creole, and youth programming at Waite House.
entries.howToUse: Arrange underwriting through its advertising page, or contact the station about community programming.

entries.name: La Raza 95.7 FM
entries.alsoKnownAs: KMNV La Raza; La Raza Minnesota
entries.what: Spanish-language radio station owned by Santamaria Broadcasting, heard on 95.7 FM and AM 1400 and streamed online. It plays Regional Mexican music and talk.
entries.howToUse: Contact its sales ("Ventas") team to advertise openings or announcements in Spanish.

entries.name: Telemundo Minnesota
entries.what: Spanish-language television station in St. Louis Park with local news, weather alerts and community segments. It reaches the Twin Cities and added signals in Duluth and Rochester.
entries.howToUse: Contact the station about its community segments; its site has a jobs ("Empleos") section under Comunidad.

entries.name: El Minnesota de Hoy
entries.what: Spanish-language digital news site for Minnesota's Latino community, published by MLatino Media. It has a "Trabajo" section for job and opportunity listings.
entries.howToUse: Advertise through its "Advertise with us" page or list openings in its Trabajo section.

entries.name: La Prensa de Minnesota
entries.what: Spanish-language news publication for the Latino community, published by LCN Media alongside Vida y Sabor and NewPrensa.
entries.howToUse: Place advertising through its "Anúnciate" page.

entries.name: Vida y Sabor
entries.what: Spanish-language entertainment and community publication for Latinos in the Twin Cities. Its classifieds include an employment ("Empleo") category.
entries.howToUse: Post job listings through its classifieds form or advertise through its "Anúnciate" page.

entries.name: Zerkalo
entries.alsoKnownAs: Zerkalo magazine; North Star newspaper; Russian Yellow Pages
entries.what: Russian-language media of Minnesota: the bimonthly Zerkalo magazine, the North Star newspaper and a Russian Yellow Pages business directory. Its classifieds include a "wanted" (job) section.
entries.howToUse: Place classified job ads, print advertising or an email blast to Russian-speaking readers.

entries.name: Korean Quarterly
entries.what: Minnesota publication covering Korean American and Korean adoptee communities, with a print edition archive, online stories and an events calendar.
entries.howToUse: Advertise through its "Advertise" link or send community news through its contact link.

entries.name: China Insight
entries.what: English-language monthly newspaper based in the Twin Cities that covers Chinese American community news and US-China connections, with an events section.
entries.howToUse: Contact the publisher through its website about advertising or event listings.

entries.name: Access Press
entries.what: St. Paul nonprofit newspaper covering disability news for Minnesotans, free in print and online. It moves to all-digital publishing on January 1, 2027, and has classifieds and a community events calendar.
entries.howToUse: Place job ads in its classifieds or display advertising, and add events through its "Add an Event" page.

entries.name: Minnesota Newspaper Association
entries.what: Trade association of Minnesota's general-interest newspapers, including small-town and rural weeklies. It runs a job bank and classifieds and statewide advertising networks that place one ad in many member papers.
entries.howToUse: Place a job or display ad through its statewide advertising networks to reach newspapers across Greater Minnesota at once.

entries.name: Minnesota Public Radio News
entries.what: Statewide public radio news service based in St. Paul, with reporting bureaus in Collegeville, Bemidji, Duluth, Moorhead, Rochester and Worthington.
entries.howToUse: Contact the newsroom or a regional bureau through the website with news about services or opportunities.

entries.name: Association of Minnesota Public Educational Radio Stations
entries.what: Association of 17 independent community radio stations across Minnesota, many in small towns and rural areas, including KAXE, KFAI, KBEM, KVSC and WTIP. It produces "North Star Stories," including a Spanish-language edition.
entries.howToUse: Contact Ampers about underwriting, where a sponsor can choose which member stations carry its message.

entries.name: KAXE Northern Community Radio
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: Northern Minnesota (Grand Rapids, Bemidji, Brainerd)
entries.what: Rural community radio station in northern Minnesota with local news and an "Events Up North" listing covering Grand Rapids, Bemidji, Brainerd and nearby towns.
entries.howToUse: Contact the station through its Contact Us page about local event listings or underwriting.

entries.name: Lakeland PBS
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: Northern and central Minnesota (Bemidji, Brainerd)
entries.what: Public television station based in Bemidji covering about 7,500 square miles of northern and central Minnesota, with a regional newscast, Lakeland News.
entries.howToUse: Send news through its "Submit a Story" form, or contact the station about its events page.

entries.name: The Somali Brief
entries.what: Digital news outlet focused on Somali Americans, launched in 2026 by Minnesota journalists. It publishes through a newsletter and social media.
entries.howToUse: Sign up for its newsletter to follow coverage, and contact it through its social media accounts.

categories.title: Community organizations, chambers and service agencies
categories.intro: Community-based organizations, mutual assistance associations, faith-based service programs, chambers of commerce and community action agencies that run programs, host events and share announcements with the people they serve. They can pass along job openings, co-host sessions and connect staff with community members.

entries.name: Minnesota Black Chamber of Commerce
entries.what: Saint Paul-based chamber founded in 2004 that serves Black-owned businesses through education, advocacy and economic development. It runs the 10,000 Black Business Program, member mixers, a small business summit and an annual gala, held in 2026.
entries.howToUse: Share openings and announcements through its newsletter and member events, or sponsor an event.

entries.name: Latino Chamber of Commerce Minnesota
entries.what: Minneapolis-based chamber launched in 2016 that supports Latino entrepreneurs. It runs a business directory, a job board, a career center, networking mixers and an annual business awards event, with some webinars in Spanish.
entries.howToUse: Post openings on its job board or attend its networking mixers.

entries.name: Minnesota Hmong Chamber of Commerce
entries.what: Saint Paul chamber that supports Hmong-owned businesses through networking, advocacy, business resources and community events.
entries.howToUse: Check its events calendar and contact the chamber about sharing openings with members.

entries.name: Minnesota Council of Churches Refugee and Immigrant Services
entries.what: Program of the Minnesota Council of Churches since 1984 that welcomes refugees and immigrants. It offers employment, case management, education and accredited immigration legal services in the Twin Cities, and employment and community navigation in Mankato.
entries.howToUse: Contact the program to share job openings with its employment services or to reach newly arrived families.

entries.name: Muslim American Society of Minnesota
entries.what: Saint Paul-based organization that runs social services, including food shelves that are open to all people regardless of religion.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organization about sharing service information with food shelf visitors.

entries.name: Mizna
entries.kind: Arab American arts and cultural organization
entries.what: Saint Paul arts organization focused on Arab and Southwest Asian and North African literature, film and art. It publishes a journal, including English and Arabic work, and produces the Twin Cities Arab Film Festival and film screenings.
entries.howToUse: Attend its public events or contact it about reaching Arab American audiences.

entries.name: Russian American Jews in Minnesota
entries.what: Organization serving Russian-speaking Jewish Minnesotans since 2003, with cultural and holiday events, teen programs and volunteer projects. It opened Teen Fellowship registration for 2026–2027.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organization about sharing announcements with Russian-speaking families.

entries.name: Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio
entries.region: Statewide: Saint Paul, Minneapolis, Willmar and Austin
entries.what: Latino-serving organization with offices in Saint Paul, Minneapolis, Willmar and Austin. It offers career training and employment, behavioral health, elder and youth programs, adult English classes and community health services, with a website in English and Spanish.
entries.howToUse: Contact its career training and employment programs to share openings, or partner on a community session.

entries.name: Hmong American Partnership
entries.what: Saint Paul organization serving Hmong and Southeast Asian American communities, including more than 25,000 immigrants and refugees. It runs HAP Academy OIC career and technical education, employment services, and benefit and health insurance navigation.
entries.howToUse: Contact its employment services to share job openings with job seekers.

entries.name: CAPI USA
entries.what: Organization serving immigrants and refugees in the Twin Cities with community advocacy, food access, workforce training and financial education. Its services moved to the CAPI Immigrant Opportunity Center in Brooklyn Center, reopened September 21, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact its workforce programs to share openings or plan an information session.

entries.name: Organization of Liberians in Minnesota
entries.what: Nonprofit founded in 1973 that serves Liberians in Minnesota with workforce development, youth and senior programs, public health education and social services from its community center in the Brooklyn Park area. It hosts Liberian Independence Day events each July.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organization to share openings or to partner on a session at its community center.
entries.dhsRecord: Listed with its website in Department of Human Services meeting minutes, February 2024: https://mn.gov/dhs/assets/february-2024ceclc-meeting-minutes_tcm1053-631685.pdf

entries.name: India Association of Minnesota
entries.what: Community association for Indian Americans in Minnesota that hosts events such as Indiafest and Gandhi Remembrance Day, held October 2, 2026, and an annual general body meeting.
entries.howToUse: Contact the association about sharing announcements or attending its public events.

entries.name: Minnesota Community Action Partnership
entries.kind: Statewide association of community action agencies
entries.what: Association of Minnesota's community action agencies, which run local anti-poverty programs in every region. Its "Find an Agency" directory lists the agency for each county.
entries.howToUse: Use its agency directory to find and contact the community action agency serving a county.

entries.name: Arrowhead Economic Opportunity Agency
entries.what: Community action agency serving St. Louis, Lake and Cook counties and nine neighboring counties with Head Start, energy and housing help, career services, senior services and transportation. It opened a new community resource center in Virginia in 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact the agency to share openings with its career services or to reach families through its programs.

entries.name: West Central Minnesota Communities Action
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: West Central Minnesota (Elbow Lake)
entries.what: Community action agency serving Traverse, Stevens, Douglas, Pope and Grant counties with energy, housing, Head Start, tax preparation, health insurance and SNAP outreach services.
entries.howToUse: Contact the agency to share service information with families in its five counties.

categories.title: Community places and gathering venues
categories.intro: Libraries, community and cultural centers, markets and event centers where people already gather. Staff can hold listening sessions, set up information tables or attend events in these places, following each venue's own rules for meeting rooms and events.

entries.name: Hennepin County Library
entries.what: Public library system with 41 locations in Minneapolis and suburban Hennepin County. Meeting rooms can be reserved up to 90 days ahead for non-social, non-commercial meetings.
entries.howToUse: Reserve a library meeting room for an information session or listening session, following the library's meeting room rules.

entries.name: Saint Paul Public Library
entries.what: Public library system with 13 branches in Saint Paul, including Rondo, Arlington Hills and Sun Ray, plus a calendar of public events.
entries.howToUse: Book a meeting room through the library's spaces page for an information or listening session.

entries.name: Ramsey County Library
entries.what: Suburban Ramsey County library system with seven locations: Maplewood, Mounds View, New Brighton, North St. Paul, Roseville, Shoreview and White Bear Lake.
entries.howToUse: Reserve a meeting room through its Meeting Rooms page for a community session.

entries.name: Great River Regional Library
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: Central Minnesota (St. Cloud area)
entries.what: Regional library system with more than 30 locations in Benton, Morrison, Sherburne, Stearns, Todd and Wright counties.
entries.howToUse: Reserve a room through its "Reserve a Room" page to hold sessions in central Minnesota towns.

entries.name: Arrowhead Library System
entries.what: Regional system based in Mountain Iron that supports member public libraries and runs a bookmobile across northeastern Minnesota.
entries.howToUse: Contact the system to reach member libraries or bookmobile stops for outreach in the Arrowhead region.

entries.name: East Central Regional Library
entries.what: Six-county library system with 14 branches, including Aitkin, Cambridge, Hinckley, Mora, North Branch, Pine City and Princeton. Meeting space varies by branch.
entries.howToUse: Contact a branch through its meeting spaces page to book a room for a local session.

entries.name: Lake Agassiz Regional Library
entries.region: Greater Minnesota: Northwest Minnesota (Moorhead, Crookston, Detroit Lakes)
entries.what: Regional library system with branches in Ada, Bagley, Breckenridge, Crookston, Detroit Lakes, Moorhead and other towns, plus smaller LINK sites.
entries.howToUse: Reserve a meeting room under its meeting room policy, for example at Moorhead Public Library.

entries.name: Plum Creek Library System
entries.what: Regional library system based in Worthington that serves public libraries in southwestern Minnesota, including Marshall-Lyon County Library.
entries.howToUse: Contact the system office to reach member libraries for outreach in southwest Minnesota.

entries.name: Southeastern Libraries Cooperating
entries.what: Rochester-based library system serving public, school and academic libraries in an 11-county region of southeastern Minnesota.
entries.howToUse: Contact SELCO to reach member libraries for outreach across southeast Minnesota.

entries.name: Brian Coyle Center
entries.what: Pillsbury United Communities center in Cedar-Riverside with a food shelf, community meals, youth internships, a career pathways program and legal clinics. Several community groups have offices there.
entries.howToUse: Call the center to ask about sharing information or holding a session with its programs.

entries.name: Hmong Cultural Center of Minnesota
entries.what: Saint Paul center with a Hmong museum, the Hmong Resource Center Library, free English and citizenship classes, and cultural arts programs.
entries.howToUse: Contact the center to partner on a session or share information with its class participants.

entries.name: Midtown Global Market
entries.what: Indoor public market on East Lake Street with immigrant-owned food and retail businesses. It hosts community events and rents event and meeting space.
entries.howToUse: Reserve event space through its "Reserve Event Space" page, or attend its public events.

entries.name: Karen Organization of Minnesota office
entries.what: Office of the Karen Organization of Minnesota in Roseville, with walk-in hours and new-arrival, employment, social, health and youth services. It hosts community flu clinics and the Karen New Year.
entries.howToUse: Contact the office to share job openings with its employment services or to plan a session with Karen community members.

entries.name: Somali Museum of Minnesota
entries.what: Museum of Somali culture in Minneapolis with monthly workshops, a Somali dance program, weaving classes and group tours. It also runs "Somali Culture 101" programs at libraries.
entries.howToUse: Contact the museum to book a group experience or partner on a community program.

entries.name: Sabathani Community Center
entries.what: South Minneapolis community center founded in 1966, one of Minnesota's oldest African American nonprofits. It offers food distribution, senior and youth programs, health, workforce and housing services, and rents event and office space.
entries.howToUse: Rent event space through its event space page, or join its community health fairs and sessions.

entries.name: Hallie Q. Brown Community Center
entries.what: Community center in Saint Paul's Rondo neighborhood, founded in 1929, with a food shelf, youth and elder programs, and community gatherings. It takes room rental requests.
entries.howToUse: Submit its reservation request form to rent space for a community session.

entries.name: HmongTown Marketplace
entries.what: Saint Paul marketplace with more than 125 Southeast Asian shops and restaurants. It holds outdoor events in its farmers market area.
entries.howToUse: Contact the marketplace about advertising or a table at one of its events.

entries.name: Saint Paul RiverCentre
entries.what: Downtown Saint Paul convention center that hosts large community events, including the Minnesota Hmong New Year and the International Festival of Minnesota.
entries.howToUse: Take a booth or attend when community festivals are held there.

entries.name: Minnesota State Fairgrounds
entries.what: Home of the Minnesota State Fair, with buildings such as the North End Event Center rented year-round outside fair season for trade shows, conferences and other events.
entries.howToUse: Use its facility rental inquiry page to rent space for a large event, or exhibit at the fair itself.

entries.name: Duluth Entertainment Convention Center
entries.what: Lakefront convention center in Duluth with ten venues and 25 meeting rooms, hosting conferences, expos and regional shows.
entries.howToUse: Contact the DECC through its meeting planner page to book space or exhibit at regional events.

entries.name: Mayo Civic Center
entries.what: Convention and entertainment venue in downtown Rochester that hosts conferences, markets and public events.
entries.howToUse: Use its event planner request page to book space or exhibit at events in southeast Minnesota.

categories.title: Recurring cultural and community events
categories.intro: Yearly public festivals and celebrations in Minnesota that draw large community crowds. Many take vendor or information booths, which gives staff a place to share openings and service information and to talk with community members where they already gather.

entries.name: Minnesota Hmong New Year
entries.what: Two-day Hmong New Year celebration at the Saint Paul RiverCentre organized by The United Hmong Family. Usual month: late November. The 45th annual event took place November 29–30, 2025, and drew more than 26,000 people.
entries.howToUse: Apply for a booth through the organizer's Hmong New Year vendor page, or attend.

entries.name: Southwest Minnesota Hmong New Year
entries.what: Hmong New Year celebration in Marshall organized by United Hmong of Southwest Minnesota. Usual month: October. The 2026 event was held October 17, 2026, at Red Baron Arena & Expo.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers about a booth or attending.

entries.name: Somali Week and Somali Independence Day celebrations
entries.what: Week of Somali cultural events tied to Somali Independence Day on July 1, centered on a Lake Street street festival. Usual month: late June to early July. The 2025 street festival was held June 28, 2025, and Somali Independence Day was celebrated again in Minneapolis in late June 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact the year's festival organizers, listed in community media guides, about a booth or attending.

entries.name: Somali Day at the Minnesota State Capitol
entries.what: Yearly gathering at the State Capitol organized by a coalition of community organizations. Usual month: April. The third annual event took place April 27, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Attend to meet community organizations taking part.

entries.name: West Side Cinco de Mayo
entries.alsoKnownAs: Cinco de Mayo Fiesta, St. Paul
entries.what: Free parade, car show and street festival on Cesar Chavez Street, held since 1985 and organized by the West Side Boosters. Usual month: early May. The 2026 festival took place May 1–2, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through the event listing about a booth, or attend.

entries.name: Soul of the Southside Juneteenth Festival
entries.what: Free Juneteenth festival at Lake Street and Minnehaha Avenue presented by the Legacy Building, with music, food, art and a Black business spotlight. Usual month: June. It took place on June 19, 2026; other Juneteenth events are held in Rondo, at the State Capitol and in St. Cloud.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through the website about a booth, or attend.

entries.name: Twin Cities Pride Festival
entries.what: Free two-day Pride festival in Loring Park with a parade on Hennepin Avenue. Usual month: late June. The 2026 festival took place June 27–28, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact Twin Cities Pride about exhibitor booths for the next festival.

entries.name: Rondo Days
entries.what: Free festival celebrating the heritage of Saint Paul's Rondo neighborhood, held on the third Saturday of July. Usual month: July. The 2026 festival took place July 18, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through the website's contact form about a booth, or attend.

entries.name: Karen New Year Celebration
entries.what: Karen New Year celebration in Saint Paul with cultural performances, speeches, sports and food. Usual month: late December or early January. Karen New Year 2765 was held January 1, 2026, at Washington Technology Magnet School.
entries.howToUse: Contact the Karen Organization of Minnesota about taking part, or attend.

entries.name: International Festival of Minnesota
entries.what: Multicultural festival with about 70 nations and ethnic communities, formerly the Festival of Nations, which returned after seven years. Usual month: April. It took place April 10–11, 2026, at the Saint Paul RiverCentre.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through the website about exhibits or volunteering, or attend.

entries.name: Vietnamese Community of Minnesota Tết Festival
entries.what: Lunar New Year festival hosted by the Vietnamese Community of Minnesota since 1981, recently at Burnsville Center, with lion dances, performances and vendors. Usual month: January or February. It took place in January 2025; the group also scheduled a Summer Festival in Bloomington for August 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact the Vietnamese Community of Minnesota about vendor space, or attend.

entries.name: ACT Disability Pride Festival
entries.what: Free festival at the Minnesota State Capitol organized by Advocating Change Together. Usual month: July. The third annual festival took place July 17, 2025.
entries.howToUse: Attend or contact the organizers about a table.

entries.name: Rochester Disability Pride Celebration
entries.what: Disability Pride celebration hosted by The Arc Minnesota, Self-Advocates Minnesota Southeast and the Region 10 Quality Council. Usual month: July. The 2026 event took place July 9, 2026, at Cascade Lake Park.
entries.howToUse: Contact The Arc Minnesota about taking part, or attend.

entries.name: Minnesota State Fair
entries.what: Twelve-day state fair ending on Labor Day, drawing visitors from across Minnesota. Usual month: late August to early September. The 2026 fair ran August 27 to September 7, 2026; the 2027 fair runs August 26 to September 6, 2027.
entries.howToUse: Apply for exhibit or vendor space through its "Become a Vendor" and exhibits pages.

entries.name: Worthington International Festival
entries.what: Free multicultural festival on the Nobles County Government Center lawn in downtown Worthington. Usual month: July. The 31st festival took place July 11–12, 2025.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through the event listing about a booth, or attend.

entries.name: Willmar International Heritage Festival
entries.what: "A Celebration of Cultures" run by Willmar Lakes Area Vision 2040 at the Willmar Civic Center. Usual month: April. The third annual festival took place April 24, 2026.
entries.howToUse: Contact Willmar Lakes Area Vision 2040 about taking part, or attend.

entries.name: Liberian Independence Day Parade and Day in the Park
entries.what: Free parade and festival in Brooklyn Park marking Liberian Independence Day, part of a weekend of events that includes an Organization of Liberians in Minnesota soccer match. Usual month: late July. The 2026 parade took place July 26, 2026, at North Hennepin Community College.
entries.howToUse: Contact the organizers through community event listings about a booth, or attend.
